gloss: to be crispy; to be irritated; to be on edge

definitions.gloss: to be crispy; to be crunchy
definitions.explanation: Describes a hard, dry crunchiness when biting into food. The texture is harder and more brittle than サクサク, like toasted bread, crispy bacon, or burnt edges.

definitions.gloss: to be irritated; to be on edge; to be worked up
definitions.explanation: Describes a state of being tense, annoyed, or short-tempered. Often used when someone is stressed and easily angered by small things.

notes:
An onomatopoeic word with two distinct meanings. The food sense mimics the sound of biting into something hard and crunchy. The irritation sense may derive from the image of scratching or scraping — a grating, tense feeling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カリカリ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧: to bake/grill until crispy
- カリカリ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{揚|あ}げる→揚げる：16879_ageru⟧: to deep-fry until crunchy
- カリカリした⟦{食感|しょっかん}→食感：06636_shokkan⟧: crunchy texture
- カリカリしないで: don't get so worked up

TEXTURE COMPARISON:
Japanese has many onomatopoeia for crunchiness, each evoking a different texture:
- サクサク: light, flaky crispness (tempura, pastry)
- カリカリ: hard, brittle crunchiness (toast, bacon)
- パリパリ: thin, snapping crispness (chips, dried seaweed)
- ⟦ザクザク→ザクザク：10956_zakuzaku⟧: rough, chunky crunch (gravel, coarse-cut cabbage)
- ポリポリ: quiet crunching (snacking on crackers)
- バリバリ: aggressive crunching (chomping through hard food)
